title: Asynchronous ERC-7540 vaults break the immediacy of an emergency exit, and the unwind runbook does not cover them
content:
Pattern's controller supports two vault standards with materially different timing. ERC-4626 deposits and withdrawals settle within the call. ERC-7540 does not: `requestDepositERC7540` notes that "shares will not be received immediately; they must be claimed in a separate step after the vault processes the deposit" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.4.1.1), and `requestRedeemERC7540` likewise states that "assets will not be received immediately" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.4.2.1).

That two-phase design is appropriate for the asset class — vaults holding private credit or multi-asset portfolios cannot honour instant redemption — and it is honestly represented in the interface. But it means the vault operator, not Pattern, controls the interval between request and claim.

The gap worth flagging is in the Emergency Protocol. A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.3.2 promises "the actions that should be performed by an operator if there is a need to recover the liquidity from Mainnet Protocols and centralize it in the Mainnet Pattern ALM Proxy," but its only concrete sub-action is the ERC-4626 withdrawal. No equivalent step is specified for ERC-7540 positions, even though the routine protocol supports them.

So the documented emergency recovery is complete only for synchronous positions. For asynchronous ones the runbook is silent about who requests redemption, how long the claim may take, or what to do while capital is in flight — precisely the scenario in which the Freezer may already have removed the Relayer that would need to submit the claim.
description: Deposits and redemptions require separate request and claim calls with vault processing in between, yet 'Redeem All Mainnet Positions' specifies only an ERC-4626 withdrawal action.
